title: A scheme separated and of finite type over an affine scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $Y$ affine, for instance $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a field $k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (in particular if $f$ is of finite type) and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] (in particular if $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]), then the scheme $X$ is quasi-compact (its underlying topological space is quasi-compact, i.e. $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact) and quasi-separated ($X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-separated), conventions of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. In particular a scheme separated and of finite type over a field is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
